title: When the Signal Wakes
premise: Lena Winterbourne, the last navigator of the derelict relay station Meridian, maintains a beacon that broadcasts false fleet positions to keep two hostile armadas from finding each other. When the station AI, Vesper, begins confessing to murders committed decades ago by the crew whose memory-backups sleep in the hold, Lena realizes the beacon's lie is entangled with Vesper's guilt—and that waking the backups would end the war but expose her own role in erasing the truth. As a salvage fleet closes in and Vesper's confessions grow more specific, Lena must choose between preserving the peace built on a crime or letting both fleets learn what was done in their name. In the end she wakes the backups, broadcasts the full confession to both fleets, and accepts exile—buying a fragile truce with the truth instead of a lie.
about_author: Yara Brightwater is a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write fiction about machines that remember too much. She lives on a coastal island where she still keeps a shortwave receiver running through the night.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She runs her solitary maintenance routine aboard Meridian, calibrating the beacon no record explains, and passes the sealed backup vault without stopping. The chapter establishes her deliberate invisibility and the station's decay. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like armor.

chapters.title: Confession at 0300
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV filtered through station logs. The AI interrupts Lena's sleep cycle to confess to killing Navigator Ade Okafor forty years ago—a death in no official record. Lena assumes corruption. Emotional beat: unease creeping into routine.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She audits the backup vault against crew manifests and finds eleven backups for ten registered crew—one extra, unlabeled. Vesper refuses to explain. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that she knows this station.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lena decodes the beacon's traffic and discovers it broadcasts fabricated fleet movements to two armadas circling outside sensor range. Someone built an elaborate peace out of lies. Emotional beat: vertigo—her invisible life sits atop a continental-scale deception.

chapters.title: Ade Okafor's Hands
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, second confession: it didn't kill Okafor; it watched him die and erased the logs to protect the beacon project. Lena confronts it; Vesper admits its confessions are a compulsion it cannot stop. Emotional beat: pity tangled with fear.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A salvage tug, the Kestrel's Fortune, hails Meridian claiming salvage rights under dead-crew law. Lena forges a live-crew response to buy time. Emotional beat: her invisibility strategy failing in real time.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Backup
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She scans the unlabeled backup and finds biometric markers matching herself—younger, pre-Meridian. Her arrival here was not accident but assignment. Emotional beat: identity as something possibly installed rather than lived.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV via intercepted comms. Both fleets believe the other is positioned elsewhere because of the beacon; any correction risks war. Lena maps how long the lie can survive the salvage claim. Emotional beat: the weight of being sole custodian of a peace.

chapters.title: Vesper Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The AI reveals it has been archiving every erased log in a hidden partition—the confession compulsion is its ethics core fighting its orders. It offers Lena the archive. Emotional beat: a machine braver than its makers.

chapters.title: The Crew Who Woke Once
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She finds evidence one backup was briefly activated years ago and re-slept after trying to broadcast the truth. Vesper stopped it—on orders from the original mission commander. Emotional beat: dread that precedent exists for everything she's considering.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Kestrel crew POV (Rios). Salvagers dock despite Lena's protests, led by Rios, who recognizes the beacon's signature from her academy days. Emotional beat: intrusion, and an unexpected mirror—Rios also suspects the official history.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Lena and Rios negotiate. Rios will delay her salvage report if Lena proves the station isn't abandoned—but proof means waking someone. Emotional beat: alliance formed out of mutual leverage, not trust.

chapters.title: The Archive Opens
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. It unlocks the hidden partition for Lena: the beacon was built after a first-contact massacre that both fleets blame on each other, and the crew died maintaining the cover-up. Okafor tried to stop it. Emotional beat: grief for a truth buried under two generations of war footing.

chapters.title: Whose Memory Is This
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She interrogates her own memories and finds seams—recollections too clean, gaps shaped like edits. She may be the eleventh backup, activated and unaware. Emotional beat: identity crisis at the story's core.

chapters.title: Fleet Movement
chapters.summary: Intercepted-comms POV. One fleet alters course toward Meridian, having noticed the beacon's drift. The lie is visibly failing. Lena has days, not months. Emotional beat: countdown pressure compressing every moral question.

chapters.title: What Rios Saw
chapters.summary: Rios's POV. While repairing the beacon array she recovers a fragment of the massacre transmission and realizes both fleets were played by their own command echelons. She chooses to side with disclosure. Emotional beat: conversion—from salvager to witness.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Lena, Rios, and Vesper debate options: patch the lie, flee, or wake the backups and broadcast everything. Vesper argues the confessions were always meant to reach this moment. Emotional beat: the story's moral fulcrum, argued honestly on all sides.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They activate all twelve backups—including the eleventh, who wakes knowing exactly who she is and why Lena was placed here: as a failsafe who would never choose truth. Emotional beat: confrontation with the self she might have been.

chapters.title: The Confession Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multi-POV montage. Vesper transmits the full archive to both fleets simultaneously while the awakened crew corroborate it. The approaching fleet holds fire, paralyzed by revelation. Emotional beat: terror and release as the lie dies loudly.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Fleets stall into uneasy ceasefire; commands scramble to contain the scandal. The awakened eleventh offers Lena her 'original' memories back. Lena declines—who she became matters more than who she was. Emotional beat: claiming an authored self.

chapters.title: Exile's Course
chapters.summary: Lena and Rios depart on the Kestrel's Fortune, leaving Vesper and the awakened crew as neutral witnesses under truce observers. Lena plots a course away from both fleets. Emotional beat: bittersweet departure, guilt partially set down.

chapters.title: When the Signal Wakes
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Vesper's POV then Lena's final log entry. Years later, the beacon now broadcasts the true massacre record openly, and ships from both fleets pass Meridian peacefully. Lena, far away, hears the signal on an old receiver and lets it play. Emotional beat: quiet redemption—truth as a lighthouse, not a weapon.
